normalization.root: stdout, stderr and symlink targets: the sandbox root (and its symlink-resolved form) is replaced by $ROOT
normalization.umask: every step runs through /bin/sh -c 'umask 022; exec ...' so the oracle and the replay create files under the same umask
normalization.passphrase: SYMVAULT_PASSPHRASE is the fixed test passphrase and SYMVAULT_ALLOW_ENV_PASSPHRASE=1; the frozen seed identities are encrypted with it
normalization.stdin: a null stdin is the null device (closed); otherwise the recorded bytes are piped and then EOF
normalization.audit_log: file audit-symvault.log: each line is parsed as a JSON object, ts/kid/hmac/argv_hash values (argv_hash digests the argv, which contains the sandbox path) are replaced by <ts>/<kid>/<hmac>/<argv_hash> (keys kept), keys are sorted, size and sha256 are taken from that normalized text
normalization.generated_archive: a *.tar.gz/*.tgz file created or changed by the command under test (its bytes differ from the pre-run state) is recorded with size -1 and sha256 <generated-archive>; its member list is compared instead
normalization.manifest: file manifest.age of the frozen vault seed: age encryption is randomised, so when a command created or rewrote it (digest differs from the seed's, or the seed has none) it is recorded with size -1 and sha256 <rewritten>; an untouched manifest keeps its exact digest, and the replay requires the same changed-or-untouched state
normalization.tar_member: tar members record name, type, header mode, content size and sha256; mtime, uid, gid, uname, gname and the tar flavour are host- or implementation-dependent and are not compared
normalization.environment: PATH=/usr/bin:/bin, HOME/USERPROFILE/XDG_* and TMPDIR inside the sandbox, NO_COLOR=1, LC_ALL=C, TZ=UTC; per-case env/unset overrides are explicit in the case
normalization.two_run_check: the generator runs every case twice against the oracle and fails when any observation differs
normalization.scope: unix recording (goos is recorded); modes, errno wording and symlink pre-state are Unix semantics
normalization.tree: per case, tree lists the nodes (path, kind, perm bits, size, sha256, symlink target) of the whole sandbox root that are new or differ from the pre-run state (seed vault, pre files, empty home/work/tmp), removed lists pre-run paths that no longer exist, archives lists the tar members of the archives in tree
normalization.stderr_tail: a case with stderr_tail_from compares stderr only up to the first occurrence of that marker (third-party age decryption wording); the marker must occur in both, and every other observation of the case stays exact

cases.desc: restore --help

results.stdout:
Restore a vault from a previously created backup archive (.tar.gz).

The archive is extracted into the current vault directory. If the vault directory
does not exist, it will be created. After extraction, the vault is verified
to ensure all expected files are present.

Usage:
  symvault restore <archive-path> [flags]

Examples:
  # Restore into the default vault directory
  symvault restore ~/symvault-2026-05-17.tar.gz

  # Restore into a custom location
  symvault --vault ~/restored restore archive.tar.gz

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for restore

Global Flags:
      --color string      When to emit ANSI color: auto, always, never (default "auto")
      --json              Output format shorthand for --output json; overrides --output when both are specified
      --no-pipe-warning   suppress 'reading from non-TTY' warning when piping secrets
      --output string     Output format (text, json, yaml) (default "text")
      --profile string    use a named vault profile
      --quiet             suppress non-error output
      --theme string      Color preset: default, highcontrast, colorblind (or SYMVAULT_THEME)
      --vault string      path to the password vault (default "~/.symvault")
